headline: OpenAI and Molecule.one advance medicinal chemistry with a near-autonomous AI chemist.

items.title: A near-autonomous AI chemist improves a challenging reaction in medicinal chemistry
items.summary: OpenAI and Molecule.one have developed a near-autonomous AI chemist using GPT-5.4 that significantly improved a key drug-making reaction. This advancement in medicinal chemistry demonstrates the potential of AI in accelerating drug discovery processes and optimizing complex chemical reactions. The AI chemist efficiently handles the synthesis of complex molecules, reducing the time and resources traditionally required. By leveraging AI, researchers can focus more on innovative drug design rather than routine synthesis tasks.
items.why_it_matters: This breakthrough can dramatically speed up drug discovery, crucial for tech leads in pharma and biotech sectors.

items.title: Introducing LifeSciBench
items.summary: LifeSciBench is a new benchmark from OpenAI, designed to evaluate AI systems on real-world life science research tasks. The benchmark is both expert-authored and reviewed, providing a robust framework for assessing AI capabilities in handling complex scientific queries and decisions in the life sciences domain. This tool aims to standardize the evaluation of AI systems' effectiveness and reliability in scientific research.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI Async Inference now supports inline request payloads
items.summary: Amazon SageMaker has introduced support for inline request payloads in its AI Async Inference feature. This enhancement allows users to send inference payloads directly in the request body of the InvokeEndpointAsync API, eliminating the need to upload input data to Amazon S3 for each invocation. This streamlines the inference process, reducing latency and improving efficiency.
